title: dynamic batching: add sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: continuous batching in the serving runtime currently groups requests primarily by arrival time and token budget which can produce batches with wide sequence length variance, leading to excessive padding and wasted compute. This PR implements a lightweight sequence-length bucketing heuristic and a padding-minimization pass that adjusts batching windows to reduce wasted tokens while keeping latency SLOs. Changes include: 1) a bucket-based sampler that tags incoming requests by estimated total sequence length (prompt + expected generation) and collects per-bucket batches up to independent budgets; 2) a padding-minimization reorder that prefers grouping requests whose lengths reduce per-batch padding without violating deadline-based SLOs; 3) minor scheduler kernel adjustments to expose per-batch sequence length to the kernel selector so we pick kernels with better memory layouts; 4) KV-cache-aware batching: we bias buckets to keep requests that will reuse similar cache shapes together to improve KV cache locality. This is implemented in src/runtime/batcher.py and scheduler-side hints in src/runtime/kernels/scheduler.cpp. Benchmark summary: - microbench (g4dn, fp16): p50 latency unchanged, p95 latency reduced by ~12-18% depending on model and seq distribution - throughput (steady-state Llama-2-13B-like workload): tokens/sec improved by ~7-10% for heterogeneous seqlen mixes - token-cost (simulated cost model): median cost/unit reduced ~8% on typical chat workloads - no regression on short-seq tail workloads thanks to deadline enforcement. Migration/rollout notes: default behavior is gated behind feature flag `dynamic_bucketing_v1` and off by default for Dedicated customers until telemetry aggregates across regions. Tests: unit tests for the bucketer and padding minimizer, and an end-to-end perf test harness under benchmarks/ci. See docs/perf/dynamic-batching.md for algorithm explanation and tuning knobs. Related: ENG-4219 (batching improvements), ENG-4370 (kv-cache locality).
